Chapter 6: Embracing Intentional Discipleship
Now that you’ve built a strong foundation of personal faith and obedience, it’s time to let your journey expand into something even greater—intentional discipleship.
This stage is all about shifting from simply growing yourself, to actively helping others grow too. Think of discipleship not as a set program, but as a way of living—where learning, modeling, and sharing just become part of who you are.
It really starts with a shift in mindset. Instead of seeing yourself just as a follower, what if you saw yourself as someone who can help others follow along as well? Imagine a relay race. The baton you carry is passed on, and your progress is connected to the encouragement and example of those both ahead of you and right behind you.
So, what are the key pieces of intentional discipleship?
First, there’s modeling authenticity. That means being real—sharing both your strengths and your struggles, so others get to see faith in action, not perfection.
Next, it’s about inviting others in. You create space for real relationships, where questions, doubts, and discoveries can be explored together. It’s about having those honest conversations, maybe over coffee, or just during a walk, where you get to learn side by side.
Then there’s offering guidance. This is about sharing what you’ve learned—your insights, your resources, your encouragement—in ways that speak to the unique journey of each person you’re walking with.
Most of the time, discipleship doesn’t look like a formal class. It’s usually informal and relational. Maybe it’s checking in regularly, being present during tough seasons, or just listening without judgment. The goal isn’t to dump a bunch of information on someone, but to actually walk alongside them, and learn from each other’s experiences.
Here’s something to pay attention to: intentional discipleship will stretch you. As you invest in others, you’ll face new challenges and questions that make you dig deeper and grow yourself. It’s a two-way street—both mentor and mentee are shaped by the relationship.
And don’t forget about community. Discipleship thrives in spaces where people feel safe to be honest, to take risks, and to celebrate progress. Small groups, study circles, or even just informal get-togethers can give these relationships the support they need to flourish.
So, what’s the big takeaway? Intentional discipleship is all about multiplication. When you choose to invest in others, your impact grows—rippling outward, creating a culture of encouragement and transformation that just keeps expanding.
